name: APT33

suspected_sponsor.note: MITRE describes APT33 as a suspected Iranian threat group.

techniques.name: Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers

description: APT33 is a suspected Iranian threat group that has carried out operations since at least 2013. The group has targeted organizations across multiple industries in the United States, Saudi Arabia, and South Korea, with a particular interest in the aviation and energy sectors.

name: OilRig

suspected_sponsor.note: MITRE describes OilRig as a suspected Iranian threat group.

description: OilRig is a suspected Iranian threat group that has targeted Middle Eastern and international victims since at least 2014. The group has targeted a variety of sectors, including financial, government, energy, chemical, and telecommunications.

name: MuddyWater

suspected_sponsor.note: MITRE cites a U.S. government assessment that MuddyWater is a subordinate element within Iran's MOIS.

techniques.name: Remote Access Tools: Remote Desktop Software
Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage

description: MuddyWater is a cyber espionage group assessed to be a subordinate element within Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS). Since at least 2017, MuddyWater has targeted a range of government and private organizations across sectors, including telecommunications, local government, finance, defense, and oil and natural gas organizations, in the Middle East (specifically the UAE and Saudi Arabia), Asia, Africa, Europe, and North America.

name: Magic Hound

suspected_sponsor.note: MITRE describes Magic Hound as Iranian-sponsored, likely operating on behalf of the IRGC.

description: Magic Hound is an Iranian-sponsored threat group that conducts long term, resource-intensive cyber espionage operations, likely on behalf of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. They have targeted European, U.S., and Middle Eastern government and military personnel, academics, journalists, and organizations such as the World Health Organization (WHO), via complex social engineering campaigns since at least 2014.

name: Molerats

suspected_sponsor.note: MITRE describes Molerats only as Arabic-speaking and politically motivated. Some vendor reporting suggests links to Hamas; treat that as unconfirmed.

techniques.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder

description: Molerats is an Arabic-speaking, politically-motivated threat group that has been operating since 2012. The group's victims have primarily been in the Middle East, Europe, and the United States.

name: Volatile Cedar

suspected_sponsor.note: MITRE describes Volatile Cedar as a Lebanese group with political and ideological motives. Vendor reporting has suggested links to Hezbollah; treat that as unconfirmed.

description: Volatile Cedar is a Lebanese threat group that has targeted individuals, companies, and institutions worldwide. Volatile Cedar has been operating since 2012 and is motivated by political and ideological interests.

name: Moses Staff

suspected_sponsor.note: MITRE describes Moses Staff as a suspected Iranian threat group.

techniques.name: Disable or Modify System Firewall: Windows Host Firewall

description: Moses Staff is a suspected Iranian threat group that has primarily targeted Israeli companies since at least September 2021. Moses Staff openly stated their motivation in attacking Israeli companies is to cause damage by leaking stolen sensitive data and encrypting the victim's networks without a ransom demand.

name: Agrius

suspected_sponsor.note: MITRE notes that public reporting has linked Agrius to Iran's MOIS.

description: Agrius is an Iranian threat actor active since 2020 notable for a series of ransomware and wiper operations in the Middle East, with an emphasis on Israeli targets. Public reporting has linked Agrius to Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS).

name: CyberAv3ngers

suspected_sponsor.note: MITRE describes CyberAv3ngers as a suspected IRGC-affiliated group, and notes that many of its claims are disputed or false.

description: The CyberAv3ngers are a suspected Iranian Government Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC)-affiliated APT group. The CyberAv3ngers have been known to be active since at least 2020, with disputed and false claims of critical infrastructure compromises in Israel.

name: Predatory Sparrow

suspected_sponsor.note: The group has no ATT&CK entry. Press and vendor reporting widely suspect state backing, but no government has confirmed it.

techniques_note: This project mapped these techniques from public incident reporting. MITRE has not published them.
description: A persona that has claimed disruptive attacks on Iranian fuel distribution, steel production and banking systems since at least 2021.

source.name: Public reporting, summarized by this project
